summary: Phase 2 real-time co-editing verified end-to-end. New backend WS suite /app/tests/test_coedit.py: 7/7 pass — editor PUT /scene broadcasts elements_synced to peer with clientId relay, scene persists via GET after PUT, viewer role gets 403 on PUT, pointer messages relay to peer only (not echoed back to sender), presence_leave relays to peer, anonymous ?share=viewer WS receives live elements_synced updates but is denied write via REST (403). Playwright two-context E2E: fresh project owned by A + B invited as editor, both browsers open /canvas/{id}, A triggers POST /simulate → B's WebSocket receives elements_batch_created with the 3 demo shapes, scene persists (GET returns count=3, types=[rectangle,rectangle,arrow]), both DOM contexts render 2 canvases each. Echo suppression works: sender's own clientId is passed through elements_synced so suppressRef ignores its own update. WS auth path in gateway (cookie/token/share/agent) is correct, engine relay of pointer/presence/presence_leave to same-canvas peers is correct.
critical_code_review_comments: ExcalidrawCanvasView: last-writer-wins is correctly implemented — /api/elements/sync clears canvas.elements and rewrites atomically; remote 'elements_synced' triggers full-scene replace via applyRemote(convertScene(...)). No incremental diffing, which matches KISS scope but means concurrent simultaneous edits from two editors will fully clobber each other for the 500ms debounce window (this is the accepted 'last-writer-wins' trade-off — call it out in docs).

Server-forced clientId echo: engine broadcasts elements_synced with clientId to ALL clients on the canvas (including the sender). Suppression is client-side via suppressRef and the CLIENT_ID check on line 115. This works but is a bit fragile — a small optimization is for the engine to skip broadcasting elements_synced back to the originating socket (like it already does for pointer/presence). Not blocking.

WebSocket proxy correctly re-authorizes via resolve_access() and additionally allows agent_token (editor) — good defense in depth. On upstream disconnect, both relay tasks are cancelled cleanly (line 789-791).
Pointer/presence relay in engine websocket.ts uses `client !== ws` to skip echoing to sender — matches test expectation that A never receives its own pointer.

MINOR: put_scene calls _hydrated.add(project_id) BEFORE the sync succeeds. If the engine sync raises, subsequent GET /scene will skip hydration and serve a stale (empty) engine cache. Consider adding _hydrated.add only after await http.post succeeds, or wrap in try/finally.

MINOR (frontend): CLIENT_ID is a module-level constant (line 10). If a user opens two tabs of the same canvas in the same browser, both tabs share the same CLIENT_ID and neither will render the other's changes because both will treat incoming elements_synced as their own echo. Move CLIENT_ID inside the component (useRef) so each mount is unique.
MINOR: onPointerUpdate throttle is 90ms which is fine; but WS_BASE is only read once at module load — safe here since REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL is baked at build time.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (2-context WS relay + simulate broadcast + persistence + read-only viewer verified)
